transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’ve been having these… strange moments. My house, or sometimes my office, just doesn’t feel real. It’s like I’m there, but also sort of watching myself from across the room. It’s been bothering me enough that I thought I should talk to someone.
How long have you been experiencing these strange moments?
About two weeks now. It started after… after a client threatened me in my office.
During these strange moments, do you see or hear anything that isn't actually there?
No… I don’t think so. It’s more that things feel off, not that I’m seeing or hearing things.
Have these strange moments been causing you significant distress or interfering with your daily life?

Yes. It’s… it’s gotten in the way. I’ve missed several client deadlines, and I stopped seeing people at the office for now. I just don’t trust myself to handle returns properly or keep things safe there.
Have you been feeling sad or empty most of the time since these strange moments started?
I don’t know… not most of the time, I don’t think. I’ve been upset, sure, but I wouldn’t call it sad or empty exactly.
Do you feel like you're disconnected from yourself or your body during these strange moments?
Yeah… sometimes. It’s like I’m there, but not really in it. Like I’m watching myself from across the room, even in my own house or at the office. It feels unreal.
Do you feel anxious or fearful when these strange moments happen?
I’m… not really sure. I get unsettled, I guess. It’s hard to say if it’s fear exactly.
Have you been having any recurring, intrusive thoughts that you can't seem to get out of your head?
I don’t think so… not like thoughts repeating over and over. I mean, my mind wanders to it sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I can’t get it out of my head.
Do you feel like you've lost touch with reality during these moments?
Kind of… not like I don’t know where I am, but my house or office feels unreal. Like I’m watching myself from across the room instead of actually being there.
Have you ever thought that someone or something is controlling your thoughts or actions?
No… I don’t think so. I haven’t felt like someone else is making me do things or putting thoughts in my head.
Can you tell me more about what happened with the client who threatened you in your office?

I remember him coming into my office and getting too close… crowding me. And I remember the police being there after.

But the part in between is… blank. What he said right before I reached for the phone, I can’t pull it up, no matter how hard I try.
Have you been avoiding people, places, or activities that remind you of the client who threatened you?
I don’t know… I haven’t really paid attention to that. I mean, I still have to go to work and deal with things. I’m not sure I’d call it avoiding.
Can you remember anything about what happened between the client threatening you and the police arriving?

Not really. I remember him crowding me in the office, and then I remember the police being there. But the middle part… what he said right before I went for the phone… it’s just blank. I can’t get it back.
Are there any other periods of time that you can't remember, besides the part after the client threatened you and before the police arrived?
No… not that I can think of. Just that part. I don’t think there are other gaps, at least none I’ve noticed.
Are there any other memories from around the time of the threat that you're having trouble recalling?

Just that same part, really. I can see him in my office, right up close, and then I can picture the police being there… but whatever happened in between, especially what he said before I reached for the phone, it’s just not there. I’ve tried, but it stays blank.
Are there any other memories or parts of your life that you feel are missing or that you cannot recall, aside from the incident with the client?
No… I don’t think so. It’s just that part with him in my office. I remember him crowding me, and then the police, but the middle—what he said before I reached for the phone—I can’t get that back.
Do you think the blank spot in your memory about what happened with the client is related to the feeling of things not being real that you've been experiencing?

I don’t know. Maybe. It’s… the same kind of strange feeling, like things aren’t quite real. Sometimes even my house or office feels off, like I’m watching myself from across the room. So maybe the blank spot is connected, but I can’t say for sure.
Have you been experiencing any physical symptoms like pain or discomfort that can't be explained by a medical condition?
Not really. I mean, nothing that I’d say is… unexplained pain or anything like that. I haven’t noticed anything specific.
Have you been experiencing any changes in your physical sensations, such as numbness or tingling, during these moments when things feel unreal?
I haven’t really noticed numbness or tingling, no. It’s more just… feeling strange or distant, I guess.
Do you think the strange, unreal feelings you've been having are more related to your thoughts and feelings or to physical sensations in your body?

More thoughts and feelings, I think. It’s not really in my body. It’s more like… my house or office suddenly feels unreal, and I feel like I’m watching myself from across the room instead of actually being there.
